features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal computer-science education the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent technical preparation is made clear.
Bachelor's-level or equivalent technical preparation is stated.
Master's-level technical preparation is stated.
Doctoral-level technical preparation is stated.

features.evidence: 3 to 7 years across 2 to 6 production services
features.name: Production engineering track record
features.description: Captures the amount and concreteness of experience testing, maintaining, and launching production software.

levels.descriptor: Production experience is vague or appears below the role's baseline.
Shows early-career production exposure, typically a few years or a small number of launched services.
Shows solid mid-level production exposure, with several years and multiple launched or maintained services.
Shows extensive production experience, with substantial tenure and repeated launch or maintenance ownership.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a core production language rather than a box-check mention.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or only incidentally named.
Go is mentioned as one language used, but without clear depth or centrality.
Go is presented as a regular production language used for meaningful work.
Go is clearly framed as a primary language, daily driver, or principal tool for shipped systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures the extent and sophistication of Python use for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent.
Python is mentioned, but only in a generic or light-use way.
Python is clearly used day to day for services, tooling, analysis, or automation.
Python is shown at production-grade depth, such as typed or tested services, major internal tooling, or core agent implementations.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing agent-based systems and the control boundaries around them.

levels.descriptor: No agentic-system experience is shown.
Agents or AI assistants are mentioned only vaguely, without design detail.
The letter shows clear experience building agent systems plus surrounding services.
The letter describes end-to-end agent architecture with explicit constraints, permissions, auditability, or guardrails.

features.name: Vulnerability automation
features.description: Captures hands-on automation of vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, or variant analysis.

levels.descriptor: No relevant vulnerability-handling automation is shown.
The letter expresses interest in security automation but gives no concrete implementation.
The letter describes building relevant automation for vulnerability handling or report triage.
The letter shows ownership of a concrete pipeline with classification, routing, deduplication, self-serve handling, or clear operational effect.

features.evidence: threat modeling with validation of fixes
features.name: Security assessment experience
features.description: Captures direct practice assessing systems for security issues rather than only building software adjacent to security.

levels.descriptor: No security-assessment work is described.
The letter suggests light exposure, such as informal reviews or broad security involvement.
The letter shows clear hands-on security assessment work on real systems.
The letter describes structured or formal assessment work, such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, and remediation follow-through.

features.name: Applied AI experience
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows real production work with AI systems, especially with reliability concerns.

levels.descriptor: No applied AI work is mentioned.
AI is mentioned only broadly or aspirationally.
The letter shows shipped AI-backed or LLM-backed features in production.
The letter shows production AI work plus explicit attention to evaluation, guardrails, predictability, or trustworthiness.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter demonstrates data-structure and algorithm skill through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of algorithmic strength is given.
The letter claims strength in algorithms or data structures without a concrete example.
The letter gives one clear example of algorithmic or data-structure improvement.
The letter gives multiple or especially strong examples tied to meaningful system simplification, performance, or correctness gains.

features.evidence: improvements inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Foundational leverage orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant understands and values internal platform work whose impact compounds across many teams.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not frame the role as platform or multiplier work.
The letter mentions scale or broad impact only in passing.
The letter clearly values foundational teams or organization-wide leverage.
The letter explicitly connects past work and future motivation to central platform impact that multiplies other teams' effectiveness.

features.name: Security engineering mindset
features.description: Captures the maturity of the letter's view of security as prevention, secure defaults, and resilient systems rather than policing or compliance.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows only generic interest in security.
The letter shows some alignment with security work, but the philosophy remains broad.
The letter expresses a clear security-engineering philosophy centered on prevention, defaults, resilience, or quiet reliability.
The letter gives a sharp, memorable articulation of security thinking that feels native to engineering practice.

features.evidence: measured hours of expert attention returned
features.name: Outcome specificity
features.description: Captures how well the letter translates activities into concrete operational results or changed team behavior.

levels.descriptor: The letter mostly lists tasks or technologies without stating outcomes.
The letter claims improvement in vague terms, with little concrete effect.
The letter states a specific operational result, such as a queue becoming routine or a bottleneck disappearing.
The letter quantifies impact or measures it in a vivid, concrete way that makes the result easy to evaluate.

features.evidence: opening thesis carried through the letter
features.name: Narrative integration
features.description: Captures whether the letter builds a coherent case for this role rather than reading like a checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads as a disconnected list of matches to the posting.
The letter is mostly list-like, with only light linking between examples and motivation.
The letter forms a coherent story that joins background, examples, and role fit.
The letter has a strong central thesis or arc that meaningfully organizes the evidence throughout.

features.name: Mechanical polish
features.description: Captures proofreading quality and sentence-level control, which matter for credibility in a careful engineering role.

levels.descriptor: Frequent distracting errors repeatedly break flow or undermine confidence.
Several noticeable errors are present and would stand out to a reviewer.
Only occasional minor errors appear, and the letter remains easy to read.
The prose is clean, with at most trivial or rare slips.
The prose is exceptionally clean and controlled throughout.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures evidence of maintaining code for external users or contributing upstream, signaling interface discipline and long-term care.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
The letter shows meaningful regular contribution or maintenance responsibility.
The letter shows sustained ownership of a project with users, releases, reviews, or roadmap responsibility.

features.name: Personal engineering ambition
features.description: Captures the technical scope and seriousness of self-directed projects used to demonstrate curiosity and systems ownership outside work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project evidence is given.
The letter mentions a small utility or simple end-to-end project.
The letter describes a moderately ambitious project chosen to learn difficult system behavior.
The letter describes a substantial project, often distributed or reliability-focused, built to confront hard edge cases.

features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows active attacker-mode practice that could sharpen security judgment.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions casual or occasional participation, with little detail.
The letter shows regular or committed participation in offensive-security exercises.
The letter shows strong placements or clearly serious, ongoing attacker-mode practice.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the rigor of third-party security certification cited as evidence of security knowledge.

levels.descriptor: No security certification or equivalent external validation is mentioned.
The letter cites a baseline knowledge credential, such as Security+.
The letter cites a stronger hands-on credential, such as OSCP.
The letter cites multiple rigorous certifications or another unusually strong form of external security validation.
